title: Branching stochastic mechanics. II. Relative localization and collective poles from Bohm/Fisher feedback
abstract: Paper I introduced branching stochastic mechanics (BSM) by lifting the Schrödinger-Nagasawa pair to reciprocal forward and backward branching fields. Their centered connected kernel $C_{\rm FB}=\mathbb E_ω[ψ_Fψ_B]$ carries the organized reciprocal sector, where $\mathbb E_ω$ denotes expectation over branching-noise realizations, with $ρ_{\rm BSM}=-C_{\rm FB}(x,x)$ on the anticorrelated branch. Here we develop the stochastic field theory of the Bohm/Fisher feedback that acts on this connected sector. Starting from the multiplicative branching covariance of BSM, a Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-de~Dominicis (MSRJD) formulation and a causal two-loop two-particle-irreducible (2PI) closure are used to determine response and correlation functions self-consistently. The free connected theory exhibits secular growth and ultraviolet accumulation, whereas the dressed theory develops a finite relative screening length. A reduced numerical evolution shows bounded formation of this localized sector, and a self-similar Fisher construction defines the saturated information velocity $c_\star$. A Born-Oppenheimer separation then distinguishes internal relative organization from collective propagation. Restoring the complete frequency structure gives two fixed-$q$ pole families: a gapless difference branch and a gapped sum branch. The infrared velocity of the difference branch approaches $c_\star$ at saturation. The common cone and the projected sum-sector gap are then formulated as additional fixed-point matching conditions for the collective theory.
summary: This work develops a stochastic field theory for Branching Stochastic Mechanics incorporating Bohm/Fisher feedback. Using advanced techniques like the MSRJD formalism and 2PI closure, the authors analyze the system's connected fluctuations. They successfully characterize the emergent dynamics by separating it into relative localization and collective propagation modes, defining key saturation velocities and pole structures.
main_problem: The paper develops a stochastic field theory to analyze the Bohm/Fisher feedback acting on the connected reciprocal sector derived from Branching Stochastic Mechanics (BSM).
main_result: The theory successfully separates dynamics into relative localization and collective propagation, yielding two fixed-q pole families: a gapless difference branch and a gapped sum branch.
method: It employs the Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-de Dominicis (MSRJD) formalism and a causal two-loop two-particle-irreducible (2PI) closure to self-consistently determine correlation and response functions.
model_or_system: The model is based on BSM, a stochastic extension of the Schrödinger–Nagasawa representation, focusing on the connected forward–backward kernel $C_{m FB}$ and the associated BSM density $ho_{m BSM}$.
key_observables: The saturated information velocity $c_\star$, the connected correlator matrix $C_{ij}$, and the two fixed-q pole families (gapless difference and gapped sum branches).
important_parameters: The relative screening length, the saturation velocity $c_\star$, and the gap/pole structure in the frequency domain.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the results of Paper I, uses the MSRJD formalism, and involves approximations like neglecting crossed physical correlators in the reduced 2PI system.

paper_structure: The paper builds upon Paper I, first establishing the stochastic field theory via MSRJD and 2PI closure. It then analyzes the reduced channels (density/phase) and separates the dynamics into relative (fast) and collective (slow) components, culminating in fixed-point matching conditions for the collective theory.
why_interesting: The use of advanced field-theoretic techniques (MSRJD, 2PI) to analyze non-equilibrium stochastic dynamics and emergent collective modes is highly relevant to understanding complex many-body systems.
